steps.description: Attacker executes a large market sell of ETH across multiple DEXs and CEXs, driving the price down from $2,000 to $1,400 (a 30% crash). This can be amplified using borrowed funds or coordinated with existing market volatility.

The oracle updates to reflect the new ETH price of $1,400. The borrower's 500 ETH collateral is now worth only $700,000 against $600,000 of debt. The health factor drops from 1.375 to 0.96 — below the liquidation threshold of 1.0.

The attacker (now acting as liquidator) calls liquidationCall to repay 50% of the borrower's debt ($300,000 USDC) and seize the equivalent collateral plus a 5% liquidation bonus. They receive ~225 ETH ($315,000 worth at current prices) for a $15,000 profit.

After the first liquidation, the borrower's remaining position is even more fragile: 275 ETH ($385,000) backing $300,000 debt. The massive collateral sale from liquidation adds further downward pressure on ETH price, pushing it to $1,200.

state_changes.cascade_risk: ⚠️ HIGH — other positions entering danger zone

steps.description: The cascading price drop triggers liquidations across many positions. Borrowers who were previously healthy (HF ~1.1–1.2) are now underwater. Each liquidation sells more collateral, further depressing the price in a death spiral. Over $20M in positions are liquidated.

After the cascade completes and ETH price is at $950, the attacker buys back ETH at the depressed price and closes all positions. They profit from both the liquidation bonuses and the price round-trip. Borrowers lost their collateral, and the protocol may have accrued bad debt from positions that couldn't be fully liquidated.

state_changes.ETH_price_recovery: Slow recovery as selling pressure subsides
